task.description: WF-03 Step 1 rework iteration 1 for ISS-0441, in response to step-01b's FAIL. Both flagged passages corrected; decisions (a)/(b)/(c) and the AC3 Step 1-4 live-verification command sequence, which the validator already passed, were left untouched.

result.summary:
Fixed both BLOCKER findings from step-01b.

(1) Consequences/AC4 grep-completeness claim: re-ran `grep -rniE --include="*.md" "hard gate|structurally impossible|Backend gate|Frontend gate" docs/` myself and opened every hit. The real complete set beyond ISS-0441's own three affected_files (0004-humanless-pipeline.md, ci.yml, GIT_MERGE.md) is NINE files, not the four originally claimed: AGENT_SYSTEM.md, WF-02_requirement_implementation.md, HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md, 0014-scripting-plugin-runtime-strategy.md (the original four) PLUS WF-01_requirement_development.md, docs/agents/protocols/GIT_SETUP.md, docs/anti-patterns.md (the three the validator flagged as missed) PLUS docs/migration/decisions/0011-frontend-ownership.md and docs/migration/decisions/0017-task-queue-selection-model.md (two more my own re-grep surfaced that neither the original design nor the validator's FAIL had named -- included them anyway since the point is an actually-complete set, not just covering the validator's specific examples). Rewrote the Consequences section to list all nine with individual one-line reasons each doesn't need correction (agent-workflow-sequencing gate / worktree-checkout limitation / historical incident narration / future-scoped S8 work / unrelated task-queue-locking claim), replacing the false 'confirmed as the complete set' language, and updated the closing 'No change is needed to...' paragraph to reference the full nine-file set instead of repeating the old incomplete three-file list.

(2) Decision (d): rewrote the enforce_admins:true rejection to stop claiming 'no override path at all'. It now explicitly acknowledges that the same admin credentials used in Step 2 can always reconfigure branch protection again (PUT enforce_admins:false, or delete the rule), merge, and optionally restore -- a real override path exists under enforce_admins:true too. The rejection is re-grounded in that path being worse for an unattended pipeline on three concrete grounds: (a) it is a multi-step sequence, not atomic -- a crash between 'disable' and 're-enable' silently leaves main unprotected for every subsequent run, whereas --admin has no partial-completion state; (b) it mutates a repo-wide setting to express what is really a per-merge judgement call, conflating 'this one red check is attributable elsewhere' with 'no check should block anyone until further notice'; (c) it is not naturally audited per merge the way --admin is visible in mergedBy/mergeCommit -- reconstructing legitimate-override-vs-forgot-to-restore requires correlating separate settings-API calls with merge timestamps, which nothing in this pipeline logs today.

Decisions (a)/(b)/(c), the Step 1-4 gh api/gh CLI command sequences (including the Step 4 live-verification plan), and the 'What this record does not decide' section were not touched -- only the two flagged passages were edited. Verified via `git diff --stat` that exactly one file changed and the diff is confined to the two passages plus the one downstream closing-paragraph consistency fix in Consequences (updating the stale three-file 'No change is needed to...' list to match the corrected nine-file enumeration above it, since leaving the old list would have reintroduced the same kind of incompleteness this rework exists to fix).
